body.x: Sierra BASE (CEO Kim Songhyun) announced its participation in CES 2025 at the K-Startup Pavilion from January 7 to 10 in Las Vegas.

The company specializes in developing autonomous drones and robots that offer 3D modeling and fully automated inspection services for infrastructure and facilities. Its proprietary technologies have been employed in over 50 structures, including 45 bridges, coal storage facilities, power plants, ports, tunnels, and steep slope cuts.

Sierra BASE is also exploring international markets, particularly Japan and the UAE. In October, the company partnered with Japanese ICT firm AQUBER to establish its presence in Japan, with notable outcomes anticipated in 2025. Following its third-place finish at the GITEX AI Challenge, the UAE market has shown keen interest, with multiple partnership requests from local companies.

At CES 2025, Sierra BASE will showcase its SIRIUS solution, an intelligent 3D autonomous robotic system. SIRIUS features multi-sensor fusion SLAM technology, utilizing rotating LiDAR for stable operations in both indoor and outdoor environments. Its precise imaging capabilities enable the detection of cracks smaller than 0.1mm, and its AI engine, trained on over 100,000 damage data points, ensures comprehensive inspection capabilities. The solution also integrates autonomous drone and robot control, AI damage detection and analysis, and web-based centralized management.

The company aims to expand into the Japanese and U.S. markets. A Sierra BASE representative commented, “Japan's focus on safety due to frequent earthquakes aligns well with our technology. We seek potential customers, partners, and investors to solidify our presence. Similarly, we hope to gain recognition in the U.S. for our capabilities, from 3D mapping to autonomous operations and safety diagnostics."

The representative added, "Exporting SIRIUS to certain countries requires navigating certification systems, which can take time. However, our web-based integrated management solution allows us to provide services like AI-powered damage analysis and reporting without delays. As certification processes progress, we plan to expand our local sales gradually.”

Sierra BASE plans to accelerate its global expansion, starting with Japan and the Middle East and then the U.S. “Our participation in GITEX revealed significant potential in the Middle Eastern market, and we are currently engaging with companies interested in local collaborations. CES 2025 will serve as our U.S. entry point, where we aim to identify business opportunities and strengthen partnerships with our existing collaborator, AQUBER,” the representative concluded.
